'''Sir Vaughan Frederick Randal Jones''' (31 December 1952{{spnd}}6 September 2020) was a [[New Zealanders|New Zealand]] mathematician known for his work on [[von Neumann algebra]]s and [[knot polynomial]]s. He was awarded a [[Fields Medal]] in 1990.

==Early life==
Jones was born in [[Gisborne, New Zealand|Gisborne]], [[New Zealand]], on 31 December 1952.<ref name=EB>{{cite encyclopedia|encyclopedia=Encyclopedia Britannica|title=Vaughan Jones (New Zealand mathematician)|url=https://www.britannica.com/biography/Vaughan-Jones|date=27 December 2019|access-date=8 September 2020|publisher=Encyclopedia Britannica, Inc.}}</ref>  He was brought up in [[Cambridge, New Zealand|Cambridge]], New Zealand, where he attended [[St Peter's School, Cambridge|St Peter's School]].  He subsequently transferred to [[Auckland Grammar School]] after winning the Gillies Scholarship,<ref name="NZH obit">{{cite news |title=Celebrated NZ mathematician Sir Vaughan Jones dies|url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=12363385|date=9 September 2020|access-date=9 September 2020|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]}}</ref> and graduated in 1969 from Auckland Grammar.<ref name="AGS obit">{{cite web|title=Obituary: Sir Vaughan Jones|url=https://www.ags.school.nz/at-grammar/news-and-messages/show/38354|date=8 September 2020|access-date=8 September 2020|publisher=Auckland Grammar School|archive-date=9 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200909052219/https://www.ags.school.nz/at-grammar/news-and-messages/show/38354|url-status=dead}}</ref>  He went on to complete his undergraduate studies at the [[University of Auckland]], obtaining a BSc in 1972 and an MSc in 1973.  For his graduate studies, he went to [[Switzerland]] where he completed his PhD at the [[University of Geneva]] in 1979.  His thesis, titled ''Actions of finite groups on the hyperfinite II<sub>1</sub> factor'', was written under the supervision of [[André Haefliger]], and won him the Vacheron Constantin Prize.<ref name="NZH obit"/>

==Career==
Jones moved to the United States in 1980.  There, he taught at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (1980–1981), and the [[University of Pennsylvania]] (1981–1985), before being appointed as professor of mathematics at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref>{{cite book |title=Who's Who in New Zealand, 1991 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6x8OAQAAMAAJ |access-date=29 July 2015 |last1=Lambert |first1=Max |year=1991 |edition=12th |publisher=Octopus |location=Auckland |page=331|isbn = 9780790001302}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Vaughan Jones - University of St. Andrews|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Jones_Vaughan/|access-date=9 September 2020}}</ref>  His work on [[knot polynomial]]s, with the discovery of what is now called the [[Jones polynomial]], was from an unexpected direction with origins in the theory of [[von Neumann algebras]],<ref name="NZH obit"/> an area of [[Mathematical analysis|analysis]] already much developed by [[Alain Connes]].  It led to the solution of a number of classical problems of [[knot theory]], to increased interest in [[low-dimensional topology]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Fields Medalist Vaughan Jones Joins the Department|url=https://as.vanderbilt.edu/math/2011/10/fields-medalist-vaughan-jones-joins-the-department/|date=25 October 2011|access-date=8 September 2020|work=Department of Mathematics|publisher=Vanderbilt University|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200909030633/https://as.vanderbilt.edu/math/2011/10/fields-medalist-vaughan-jones-joins-the-department/|archive-date=9 September 2020}}</ref> and to the development of [[quantum topology]].

Jones taught at [[Vanderbilt University]] as Stevenson Distinguished Professor of mathematics from 2011 until his death.<ref>[http://as.vanderbilt.edu/math/bio/vaughan-jones Personal web page at Vanderbilt University]</ref>  He remained Professor Emeritus at University of California, Berkeley, where he had been on the faculty from 1985 to 2011<ref>[https://math.berkeley.edu/people/faculty/vaughan-f-r-jones His Past Faculty web page at Berkeley]</ref> and was a Distinguished Alumni Professor at the [[University of Auckland]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://unidirectory.auckland.ac.nz/profile/v-jones |title=Personal web page at Auckland |access-date=12 December 2015 |archive-date=22 December 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222104615/https://unidirectory.auckland.ac.nz/profile/v-jones |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Jones was made an honorary vice-president for life of the [[International Guild of Knot Tyers]] in 1992.<ref name="AGS obit"/>  The Jones Medal, created by the [[Royal Society Te Apārangi|Royal Society of New Zealand]] in 2010, is named after him.<ref name="Jones Medal">{{cite news|title=About the Jones Medal|url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/what-we-do/medals-and-awards/jones-medal/about-the-medal-3/|access-date=8 September 2020|publisher=Royal Society Te Apārangi|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200909032945/https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/what-we-do/medals-and-awards/jones-medal/about-the-medal-3/|archive-date=9 September 2020}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Jones met his wife, Martha Myers, during a ski camp for foreign students while they were studying in Switzerland.<ref name=Salisbury>{{cite news|title=Vaughan Jones – Fields medalist brings informal style to Vanderbilt|url=https://news.vanderbilt.edu/2011/10/03/new-faculty-vaughan-jones/|first=David|last=Salisbury|date=3 October 2011|access-date=8 September 2020|publisher=Vanderbilt University|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200714101000/https://news.vanderbilt.edu/2011/10/03/new-faculty-vaughan-jones/|archive-date=14 July 2020}}</ref>  She was there as a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright scholar]],<ref name=Salisbury/> and subsequently became an associate professor of medicine, health and society.<ref name="AGS obit"/>  Together, they have three children.<ref name="NZH obit"/><ref name="AGS obit"/>

Jones died on 6 September 2020 at age 67 from health complications resulting from a severe [[ear infection]].<ref>[https://as.vanderbilt.edu/math/2020/09/department-of-mathematics-mourns-the-passing-of-stevenson-chair-and-distinguished-professor-vaughan-jones/ Release of Vanderbilt University] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210831145153/https://as.vanderbilt.edu/math/2020/09/department-of-mathematics-mourns-the-passing-of-stevenson-chair-and-distinguished-professor-vaughan-jones/ |date=31 August 2021 }}, 8 September 2020.</ref><ref name="NZH obit"/>

Jones was a certified barista.<ref>{{Citation |title=Vaughan Jones: "God May or May Not Play Dice but She Sure Loves a von Neumann Algebra" | date=10 May 2018 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k3AtJ7wQKsk |access-date=2023-03-14 |language=en}}</ref>

== Honours and awards==
* 1990{{snd}}awarded the [[Fields Medal]]<ref name="NZH obit"/>
* 1990{{snd}}elected [[Fellow of the Royal Society]]<ref>{{ cite web | url= http://royalsociety.org/about-us/fellowship/fellows/|title = Fellows |publisher=Royal Society|access-date = 5 November 2010}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Evans |first=David E. |date=2022 |title=Sir Vaughan Jones. 31 December 1952—6 September 2020 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |volume=73|pages=333–356 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2021.0051 |s2cid=249648564 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
* 1991{{snd}}awarded the [[Rutherford Medal (Royal Society of New Zealand)|Rutherford Medal]] by the [[Royal Society of New Zealand]]<ref name="AGS obit"/><ref name="Jones Medal"/>
* 1991{{snd}}awarded the degree of [[Doctor of Science]] by the [[University of Auckland]]<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bKQUAQAAMAAJ&q=%22vaughan+jones%22+%22honorary+doctorate%22|title=The New Zealand Official Year-book|volume=95|author=Department of Statistics|publisher=Government Printer (New Zealand)|year=1992}}</ref>
* 1991 – elected Honorary Fellow of the Royal Society of New Zealand<ref>{{Cite web |title=J-L |url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/who-we-are/our-people/our-fellows/all-honorary-fellows/j-l/ |access-date=2024-03-25 |website=Royal Society Te Apārangi}}</ref>
* 1992{{snd}}elected to the [[Australian Academy of Science]] as a Corresponding Fellow<ref>{{cite news|title=Faculty Awards|url=https://as.vanderbilt.edu/math/research/facultyawards/|access-date=8 September 2020|work=Department of Mathematics|publisher=Vanderbilt University}}</ref>
* 1992{{snd}}awarded a [[Miller Institute|Miller]] Professorship at the University of California Berkeley<ref>{{cite news|title=Celebrating Science – Miller Reminiscences|url=https://miller.berkeley.edu/about/reminiscences|access-date=8 September 2020|work=Miller Institute|publisher=University of California, Berkeley}}</ref>
* 2002{{snd}}appointed [[Distinguished Companion of the New Zealand Order of Merit]] (DCNZM) in the [[2002 Birthday Honours (New Zealand)|2002 Queen's Birthday and Golden Jubilee Honours]], for services to mathematics<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dpmc.govt.nz/publications/queens-birthday-and-golden-jubilee-honours-list-2002 |title=Queen's Birthday and Golden Jubilee honours list 2002 |date=3 June 2002 |publisher=Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet |access-date=25 June 2020}}</ref>
* 2009{{snd}}his DCNZM redesignated to a [[Knight Companion of the New Zealand Order of Merit]] in the [[2009 Special Honours (New Zealand)|2009 Special Honours]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dpmc.govt.nz/publications/special-honours-list-1-august-2009 |title=Special honours list 1 August 2009 |date=5 April 2011 |publisher=Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet |access-date=25 June 2020}}</ref>
* 2012{{snd}}elected a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]]<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |date=25 August 2018 }}, retrieved 26 January 2013.</ref>
